sourceReviewResult: R80 links confirmed food-grade dried Ferula gum resin to four candidate FSSAI spice articles. The 2025 Chapter 2.9 compendium reproduces the 11 earlier grade-specific purity values. Five FSSAI laboratory methods and the Indian Standard starch method now have page references.

spiceBoard.title: Spices Board commodity profile for asafoetida
spiceBoard.description: The Board describes the spice as dried latex from the underground Ferula rhizome or taproot.

methods.detail: The manual reports percentage by mass and offers a separate moisture-free calculation. Record the basis reported by the laboratory.
The method measures the acid-insoluble portion of the ash. It gives a mass percentage and an optional moisture-free conversion.
Use the asafoetida-specific note on PDF page 33. The adjacent general spice calculation uses a dry basis. Clause 2.9.29 cites U.S.P. 1936.

methods.parameter: Galbanum, ammoniacum and other foreign resins
methods.detail: Qualitative tests. The interpretation for other foreign resins differs between natural and compounded asafoetida.
A separate qualitative thin-layer chromatography test uses abietic acid as the marker. It has no numeric contaminant threshold.
After microscopic evidence of added starch, clause 8 specifies enzymatic estimation with diastase. The compounding assumption in the archived calculation is specific to wheat flour.

matrixNote: Confirm the supplied spice is natural dried gum resin exuded from Ferula roots or rhizomes. Powdered root, an extracted oil and a mixture with starch, flour or gum arabic each need a separate assessment.
